messages:
Alex: Hey team — finishing onboarding and have a quick Vault/KMS question: what's our preferred flow to request a secret for a new service (staging -> prod), who needs to approve prod access, and any simple rotation basics I should follow? Thanks!

DevEx Bot: Hi @Alex — onboarding checklist here: https://redwood.dev/docs/devex/vault-onboarding. For secret requests open a help ticket in #help (use the vault-request template). Prod requests require an approver from your product/infra lead. :white_check_mark:

Sara: Hey Alex — TL;DR steps: 1) Open a help ticket with the vault-request template or create a GH issue; 2) Include service id, owning team, target env(s), secret path you want, intended TTL/rotation cadence, and whether the secret should be KMS-wrapped or dynamic; 3) Indicate who should approve prod access. For static API keys we provision paths like secrets/teams/<team>/<service>/<env>/<name>. For DB credentials we prefer dynamic DB creds via Vault's DB plugin — put that in the ticket.

Sara: Example (dev-only KV v2):
```
# dev example (KV v2)
vault kv put secret/teams/myteam/myservice/staging api_key=\"REDACTED\"
```

Sara: Approval rules: production secret requests need a named approver (product manager or infra owner). Emergency prod access can be escalated to oncall infra. Rotation basics: set an "owner" in the ticket/metadata, prefer dynamic creds where possible (Vault DB), for static keys schedule automated rotation (we aim monthly for user-facing API keys unless otherwise noted), and use vault-agent or the SDK to fetch secrets at runtime so you don't bake secrets into images.

Chen: Quick Q — for encryption keys do we default to AWS KMS CMKs or use Vault Transit? Which should I request?

Sara: Use AWS KMS CMKs for long-lived key material (e.g., encrypting backups, long-term blobs) — we have team CMK aliases like alias/redwood-prod-<team>. Use Vault Transit for short-lived signing/encrypting of ephemeral payloads and token wrapping. If you need a customer-managed CMK, note it in the ticket and include the KMS key ARN.

Jordan: One gotcha: if your service runs in GCP, request IAM-auth-enabled mounts and include the GCP project id + service account email in the ticket so we can configure the auth role mapping.

Alex: Great, that clarifies it. I'll open the ticket and use the template, and I'll ping @Sara for prod approval once the ticket is up. Thanks!

DevEx Bot: Ticket template: https://redwood.dev/internal/templates/vault-request. If you want help drafting the ticket, DM @Sara or drop the draft here and we'll help edit. :raised_hands:
